name: Blue Mountains National Park
step: Quill step 1 research (facts only, no copy)

what_it_is.fact: World Heritage-listed national park (2,679.54 km2, managed by NSW National Parks and Wildlife Service) on Sydney's doorstep; nearest city Katoomba. It is the most central of eight protected areas in the UNESCO Greater Blue Mountains Area (inscribed 2000). Katoomba is about 103 km / ~1h50 by road west of Sydney. Visitor district centres on Katoomba, with Echo Point, Scenic World, Wentworth Falls and Leura within a few km; Blackheath and Mount Victoria are ~15 min drive away. Over 140 km of tracks and trails.
what_it_is.extra: Wikipedia gives 8,438,671 visits (2018 figure in infobox); Secret Sydney (Apr 2026) says it sees more foot traffic than any of the state's 200-plus parks. Wikivoyage warns not to type 'Blue Mountains' into a GPS: it routes to the park centroid on unpaved roads; use 'Echo Point, Katoomba'.

proposed_fields.rank_reason: COVERAGE.md table: 'country highlight a guidebook gives top billing' (Christchurch/Abel Tasman tier). NPWS and Wikivoyage lead with it; most-visited NSW park; Sydney's headline day trip. Not rank 1 (not on most whole-country itineraries like Uluru/Great Barrier Reef). Judgement call.

whyVisit_candidates.reason: Echo Point and the Three Sisters over the Jamison Valley
whyVisit_candidates.facts: Echo Point is the most popular attraction near Katoomba, a major lookout over the Jamison Valley and the Three Sisters; the park is 'renowned for the Three Sisters rock formation'. Parking at Echo Point is paid (about $8/hour per Wikivoyage); Wikivoyage suggests parking free at Scenic World and walking.
whyVisit_candidates.photo_hint: Placement accepted Commons 'Australia new Katoomba the three sisters.jpg' (sunrise, Echo Point) for the Echo Point spot; why-visit photo must differ from the header and the spot photo.

whyVisit_candidates.reason: Ride the Scenic Railway and Skyway at Scenic World
whyVisit_candidates.facts: Scenic World (Katoomba) markets the Scenic Railway as the world's steepest passenger railway, a 52 degree incline into the rainforest; also Scenic Skyway over the Jamison Valley, Scenic Cableway and Scenic Walkway. Hours on its site: 9 AM - 5 PM. Ticket prices seen on its homepage: $64 and $120 (which products these map to NOT verified; check the tickets page before using). 'World's steepest' is the operator's own claim: attribute or soften.
whyVisit_candidates.photo_hint: Placement accepted Commons 'Katoomba (AU), Scenic World, Scenic Skyway -- 2019 -- 1872.jpg' for the Scenic World spot (so use a different file here, e.g. the railway).

whyVisit_candidates.reason: Walk the cliff-edge tracks and waterfalls (Wentworth Falls, Grand Canyon, Giant Stairway)
whyVisit_candidates.facts: NPWS: 140 km of tracks; Wentworth Falls has lookouts, walks and waterfalls; the Grand Canyon descends into a canyon; Grand Cliff Top Walk is 19 km Wentworth Falls to Leura to Katoomba over 2 days. Wikivoyage: Giant Stairway descends beside the Three Sisters; valley floor walk ~2 km to Scenic World, then back up on the Scenic Railway (loop via Prince Henry Cliff Walk). Caution: several of these are currently closed (see tips); the Giant Stairway/Echo Point loop and Grand Canyon from Evans Lookout are not listed as closed in the NPWS alert text I read, but confirm on the alerts page before writing a specific walk into copy.
whyVisit_candidates.photo_hint: Wentworth Falls or Grand Canyon (rainforest canyon); distinct from Echo Point photo.

whyVisit_alternates: Govetts Leap / Grose Valley wilderness cliffs at Blackheath (NPWS: 'sweeping views of sheer sandstone cliffs and hazy blue Grose Valley declared wilderness area from Govetts Leap'; Wikivoyage: 'fantastic views over the Grose Valley'). Use if the walks reason is too tied to closed tracks. NOTE: Govetts descent is currently closed (valley access from Blackheath via Horse Track), but the lookout itself is not listed as closed.

goodToKnow_candidates.tip: Track and area closures are common and some are long-term: Jenolan Karst Conservation Reserve (incl. Caves Visitor Precinct) and the Six Foot Track boundary are closed until 31 Dec 2026; part of National Pass (west of Wentworth Falls middle crossing) is closed after a major landslide with no reopening date; Honeymoon Bridge, Lindeman Pass (part), Roberts Pass, Wentworth Pass, Slack Stairs, Valley of the Waters below Sylvia Falls and Govetts descent are closed; Lower Fern Bower track closed until 30 Oct 2026; Mt Hay Road and its tracks closed 9 June - 17 Dec 2026. Check NPWS alerts before setting out.
goodToKnow_candidates.note: Closure dates are as of 16 Oct 2026 and change; copy should say 'check the NPWS alerts page' rather than hard-code dates that will go stale. Do not list Jenolan as a reason to visit. Also: Wikivoyage's own 'National Pass closed due to rockfall' matches the NPWS partial closure; the full loop is not walkable.

goodToKnow_candidates.tip: Trains from Sydney Central run roughly hourly (half-hourly in peak) to the mountains, no seat reservations, and take about 2 hours to Leura/Katoomba; most towns are linked by rail but Wentworth Falls, Leura Cascades, Govetts Leap and others need a bus, taxi or car. Local bus 686 links Katoomba station, Echo Point and Scenic World every 30 minutes and takes Opal; Opal daily cap means local buses may cost nothing extra on a day trip from Sydney.
goodToKnow_candidates.unverified: Exact current train time and Opal cap were NOT checked on transport.nsw.gov.au (the page fetched was a generic homepage). Wikivoyage Leura says 'about a 2-hour train trip, depending on delays' and Katoomba 'usually hourly' (Wikivoyage text dated 2026 for fares). Verify on transport.nsw.gov.au before shipping a number.

goodToKnow_candidates.tip: Check the weather before choosing the day: the mountains can be up to 10 C colder than the coast, and on cold rainy winter days fog can hide the views all day (Wikipedia's Echo Point caption notes fog over the Jamison Valley is a common feature). Also, GPS: search 'Echo Point, Katoomba' not 'Blue Mountains'.

goodToKnow_other_options: Carry supplies and tell someone your route: some cliff walks have no mobile coverage and people have died after losing the trail; free personal locator beacons from Katoomba Police for remote walks (Wikivoyage Blue Mountains, Stay safe).
Fire bans: NPWS page shows 'Fire bans' among the park's alerts (Oct 2026); bushfire danger in summer is a real recurring pattern but I did not find a sourced description beyond the alert header.

seasons.bestMonths_note: Only autumn (Mar-May) is supported by sources I read. Secret Sydney (20 Apr 2026): autumn brings cooler weather, quieter trails and changing colour. The search summary cited a guide putting peak foliage late April to mid-May, and Mount Wilson/Blackheath/Leura estates for colour, but I did not load that page (Traveller article would not yield text; championtraveler.com not fetched). Wikivoyage Blue Mountains: Mount Wilson (private botanic gardens known for autumn colours) and Oberon known for autumn colours. Spring (Sep-Nov) is plausible but unsourced here: UNVERIFIED, so left out of bestMonths_proposed; owner may add [9,10,11].
seasons.bestTimeBlurb_source: https://secretsydney.com/blue-mountains-national-park-autumn/ and https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Blue_Mountains (climate). Draft basis only: autumn ({months}) for cooler walking weather and colour in the Mount Wilson, Leura and Blackheath area; winter is cold with fog and snow only once or twice every year or two (Wikivoyage: 'one or two days of snow every one or two years'); summer weekends fill car parks at Wentworth Falls (Wikivoyage).
seasons.seasonalTags: Yulefest (Christmas-in-July) is a real annual pattern: Secret Sydney says it is held throughout July 2026 across Katoomba, Leura, Blackheath, Mount Victoria with festive menus at hotels and restaurants. Another listing gave July/August (unverified, from a search snippet). Suggest a seasonalTag for July only if the owner wants it; per COVERAGE.md it is an event, so mention in best-time text rather than as a spot. Source: https://secretsydney.com/blue-mountains-yulefest-2026/
seasons.hemisphere: Southern: summer Dec-Feb, autumn Mar-May, winter Jun-Aug, spring Sep-Nov.
